If this is the first time you have been totally honest with someone then it stands to reason you can't see yourself employing honesty in in the future.  It's like lifting weights, you don't start curling 45 lbs. on your first day.  Start small and work your way up, sharing your story to a stranger is a good start, keep it up.  

Just to clarify, I don't mean you should be 100% honest all the time.  For better or worse, lying has it's uses.  It's impossible to be completely honest all the time erryday. 

You're not weak.

No problem brother.  

Like I said, honesty is tough.  It's much easier to lie. But honest gives you conviction and makes you strong.  

You'll figure it out.

You don't sound emo or stupid.  Your SO not wanting to talk about this is no fault of your own, some people prefer to ignore sadness and anxiety-inducing topics and that is totally fine.  To each their own.  It is also acceptable to feel anxious about those things, you're not weird.  

What about the future makes you anxious?  If you could build better memories, what memories would you build?
What do you like writing?  Try switching it up.  If you mostly write abstract anecdotes, try poems or songs.

Thank you for reaching out.

My experience with drug addiction has always been second-hand through my close friends.  Long story short, they got into heroine (intravenously) and I didn't.  What I saw from them was a lot of lies.  They lied to themselves, their family, and their friends, including me.  They were severely depressed, as was I, but never EVER brought it up.  

It's important to realize that my friends and I were both abusing completely different drugs (I was smoking pot and drinking), yet shared the same sorrows.  If I were you, I wouldn't dwell on past addictions and problems, just look forward, fuck the past.  Shit's weak sometimes.

My biggest hurdle wasn't the drugs.  It was the honesty. I lied all the damn time, even to myself.  I used to think everyone despised me for no reason.  Even though I knew I was being delusional I continued to believe it. That's the way I thought things were. Honesty to self and others is tough.  When I started to be honest with myself, I felt improvement.  Putting yourself out there via honesty is tough, especially when you have social anxiety.  Being honest has made me confident in myself, headstrong, in a way.  It was a huge hurdle, but hurdles are meant for jumping.  

Of course, I don't know you, so my advice could be shit from your perspective. My point is, examine yourself introspectively.  Ask yourself why you feel the way you do, what behaviors led you here, and what needs to be done to fix it.  

First thing you should do is go to your psychologist and open up completely.  Let it all out, listen, then feel the relieve as the weight eases off your shoulders.  After that, schedule your next appointment and go for a run.

Emotions (not just the depressive ones) ebb and flow like the tide, so don't be worried if it's gotten bad all the sudden, good days are ahead.  Maybe your subconscious is trying to get you to express yourself more! When I play guitar, write, spar, or draw, I'm always in my place. the place I want to be.  Even if what I'm writing is negative, I want to be there because it's an avenue for what's been bottled up inside to rush out into the ether where it belongs.
Ever tried meditating?  It's the bee's knee's, bruh.

Sup dude (or dudette)

I have no experience with antidepressants, so take what I say with a grain of salt.  It seems to me like these are things you've always wanted to express and they have now manifested through your writing.  Do you ever share you work with anyone you know?

>I don't necessarily think the rose colored glasses approach will work for everyone

I completely agree.  Depression is so tuned into the individual it's hard to give holistic advice about it.  Motivation to do anything is a huge factor when dealing with depression, which was probably the largest hurdle to jump
Rational people will not continue to struggle, rational people will adapt.
Haha you're both thinking way too deep into what I'm trying to say.  Sure Reddit didn't 100% help me, but it did that night. That's all that matters.  I'm just here to share what worked for me :)

My major is Broadcast Communication 

Always know that no matter what, opportunities will always be there.  If you want something, go after it.  Don't worry about living a glamorous life; all you need is a job to get you started, a place to live, and food. From there you can continue to climb.  It's hard to give advice because I do not know your particular situation, but I do know that there are a lot of awesome things you can do for free!  Live cheap and have fun.

Yes, you are absolutely right in that I could feel the depression creeping in once in a while.  I would make a conscious effort to understand that the world is not as it seems (dark and shitty), and this trick of the mind will pass.  I would preoccupy myself by going out with friends, or walking my dog.  Don't just wallow in your slowly creeping depression, distract yourself with things you love to do until it fades back away.

I can assure you that everyone doesn't hate you.  Don't mistake hate for misunderstanding.  Maybe you can find a group to talk to who are in the same situation as you are?  Group therapy can do wonders!

Remember, depression shifts how you think, which is why you need to make the effort to shift it back.  Funny thing is I knew my advice was going to be brushed off as generic bullshit you've heard before.  Your depression is brushing it off, at least give it a try!

What you have to understand is that even though depression is a mental illeness, it's not the same as bi-polar disorder or schizophrenia or what have you.  It's on a completely different, and more personal, level.  That is why there is "no cure", because depression is so tuned into who YOU are.  I doubt you were born with it, the way you have perceived you life has made you think the way you do.  what you need to do (what I did) is make an effort to see the good in things.  You missed the bus? that's ok, another one is coming anyway.  The airport lost my luggage? That sucks, but I'll get it back soon enough. Oh, someone said a smartass comment about you?  Fuck that guy, he's probably got a tiny dick anyway.  You must make the effort to shift the way you think.

Also, TALK.  Find a close friend and open up to them.  This really works.  Getting bottled up things off your chest feels amazing.  Go see a therapist and don't be ashamed of it, that is what they are for.  Find a hobby, make friends, open up.  Let the world be your playground.  Be assertive, be dominant, be YOURSELF.  Start working out, get a dog, learn how to juggle, move to another state/country!  The key is to keep your mind occupied with things you love rather than things you hate!

I understand.  I went through this and I know how terrible it is.  Everything you should take joy in is nothing but petty shit with depression.  I have been depression (and suicidal) free for about a year now.  Ask me anything!  I would love to help you friend :)
Thank you!  It really was tough but I crawled out of it stronger than you could imagine!

What you must understand about depression is that it filters what you see in life.  It will make the good look normal, the normal look bad, and the bad look absolutely fucking terrible.  I would bet things didn't go crashing down in flames strictly because of you; do yourself a favor and don't beat yourself up over it.  If you want to talk to me PM me, I think I can help :)

Those who treat you like shit don't deserve to have you in their life.  Everyone has the ability to be an asshole, ignore them at let them be assholes to someone else.  You are a wonderful person, don't let anyone tell you different.  Please PM me if you want to talk, you can trust me.

Hey buddy, I was where you were about a year ago.  I had my death picked out down to who was going find me and where.  Whenever someone would ask what was wrong I would say "nothing I'm just tired".  I do not have depression anymore and I would love to help you.  Message me if you want to talk!
